{{Short description|Words that denote non-numerical quantities}}
{{Orphan|date=March 2021}}

The English language has a number of [[word]]s that denote specific or approximate [[Quantity|quantities]] that are themselves not [[number]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-11-12|title=Non-numerical words for quantities ⋆ Annie Non-numerical words|url=https://www.annemiekdunhof.com/english-grammar-clarifications/non-numerical-words-for-quantities/|access-date=2021-03-22|website=Annie|language=en-GB}}</ref> Along with numerals, and special-purpose words like some, any, much, more, every, few, several, and all, they are [[Quantifier (linguistics)|quantifier]]s. Quantifiers are a kind of determiner and occur in many constructions with other determiners, like articles: e.g., two dozen or more than a score. Scientific non-numerical quantities are represented as [[International System of Units|SI units]].
